title: DADI 1H (NSIC Rc 786H) Hybrid Rice: Characteristics and Grain Quality
metaTitle: DADI 1H (NSIC Rc 786H): Characteristics and Grain Quality
metaDescription: DADI 1H is NSIC Rc 786H, a hybrid rice for irrigated lowland approved in 2026. See its pest ratings, grain quality and where it grows best.
excerpt: NSIC Rc 786H is a hybrid rice variety for irrigated lowland, sold as DADI 1H and known locally as Mestiso 157. The NSIC approved it in 2026. Philippine Dadi Agricultural Technology bred it. PhilRice has not listed its days to harvest and trial yield yet, but its pest ratings and grain quality are below.

heroImage.alt: Ripe palay heads, the harvest a hybrid like NSIC Rc 786H is bred to fill

blocks.text: If you came here looking for DADI 1H, or rice variety 786H, this is the one. The facts below come from sources that include PhilRice and its public seed database. So you can compare it with the other varieties in our [rice variety finder](/rice-varieties) before you buy seed. Also read our guide to [rice varieties in the Philippines](/crops/rice-varieties-philippines) for how inbreds, hybrids and special rice differ.

items: **Holds up against:** stem borer, rice blast.
**Watch out for:** green leafhopper, brown planthopper, tungro.
**Cooked rice:** low amylose, so soft and tender.

blocks.text: How many days does it take, and how much does it yield?

PhilRice has not published this variety's days to harvest and trial yields in its catalogue yet. So ask the seed seller or your municipal agriculturist for the figures from the trials in your region before you plan the season. Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with the [growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it. Meanwhile, our guide to [raising rice yield per hectare](/blog/increase-rice-yield-per-hectare) covers the habits that matter with any variety.

blocks.text: So scout early for [green leafhopper](/pests/green-leafhopper), [brown planthopper](/pests/brown-planthopper), [tungro](/diseases/rice-tungro). When you see the first signs, check the guide before you spray, because the right timing saves more than an extra dose. If you are not sure what you see, our [pest and disease finders](/features/pest-and-disease-finders) help you name it from the damage.

blocks.caption: Grain quality in PhilRice's seed database

blocks.text: Amylose decides how rice cooks. With low amylose, expect rice that is soft. In fact, PhilRice notes that Filipino taste moved from high to intermediate and low amylose rice, because people want it softer.

It suits irrigated lowland, where you control the water. Level the field well so the water stands evenly, and plant at the same time as your neighbors, one of the PalayCheck key checks, so pests cannot move from field to field. Our guide to [rice land preparation](/land-preparation/rice-land-preparation) shows each step. For the right month in your province, see [the best time to plant rice](/blog/best-time-to-plant-rice-philippines).

items.q: Is DADI 1H the same as NSIC Rc 786H?
items.a: Yes. DADI 1H is the name it is sold under, and NSIC Rc 786H is its registration with the National Seed Industry Council, where its local name is Mestiso 157. The numbers on this page are PhilRice's for NSIC Rc 786H.

items.q: What is the local name of NSIC Rc 786H?
items.a: It is known as Mestiso 157. Seed sellers and agriculturists use both names, so ask for either one.
The NSIC approved it in 2026. Philippine Dadi Agricultural Technology bred it. PhilRice has not listed its days to harvest and trial yield yet, so ask for the regional trial figures before you plant.
Yes. So buy new seed each season, because seed saved from a hybrid crop does not grow true and yields less.

items.q: What should I watch for when I plant it?
items.a: In PhilRice's tests it was weak against green leafhopper, brown planthopper, tungro. So scout from the early weeks and act at the first signs.
It has low amylose, 12.7 percent. So it cooks soft.
